uncited: Generative and Style-based Models extend the NeRF paradigm from reconstructing a single static scene to synthesizing novel, high-fidelity 3D-consistent images from a distribution of scenes.

They solve the problem of limited training data and the inability of standard NeRF to generalize across a class of objects (e.g., all faces or all cars) by conditioning the radiance field on a latent code.
Unlike standard NeRF, which optimizes weights for a fixed scene, these models learn a mapping from a latent space to the scene geometry and appearance, enabling the generation of new instances.

They are distinguished from siblings like [AdaNeRF](6195-adanerf.md) and [SinNeRF](6199-sinnerf.md) by their explicit use of generative priors (GANs, Diffusion) and style-based conditioning to control appearance attributes and ensure multi-view consistency without requiring explicit 3D supervision.

All methods in this family share the mechanism of mapping 6D input coordinates (3D position $\mathbf{x}$ and 2D viewing direction $\mathbf{d}$) to 4D output values (density $\sigma$ and color $\mathbf{c}$) using a differentiable neural network.
This allows the radiance field to be optimized through the volumetric rendering integral.
Raw coordinates $\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{d}$ are rarely used directly due to the spectral bias of MLPs, which struggle to fit high-frequency details.
**Density Network:** Takes the encoded position $\gamma(\mathbf{x})$ as input.

**Color Network:** Takes the encoded position $\gamma(\mathbf{x})$, the raw viewing direction $\mathbf{d}$, and the intermediate feature vector from the density network (usually the output of the last hidden layer before the density head) as input.
During training, rays are sampled at points $\mathbf{x}_i$ along the ray.
Here, $z$ is the input over all timesteps, $G(z)$ is the generated result, $D(x)$ is the discriminator score for real data $x$, and $x$ is replaced by $G(z)$ for fake data.
Early works like [GRAF](9572-generative-and-style-based-models.md) and [pi-GAN](10298-pi-gan.md) introduced GAN-based frameworks to learn 3D-aware representations from 2D images.

Subsequent developments such as [StyleNeRF](8659-stylenerf.md) and [HyperNeRFGAN](8765-hypernerfgan.md) incorporated style-based generators and hypernetworks to improve resolution and controllability.
More recent approaches like [Latent-NeRF](9110-latent-nerf.md) integrate diffusion models for high-fidelity detail synthesis.
